text:
jamie: Quick sync — proposing a smaller-scope split of the control plane: keep control API in regional VPCs, but centralize auth and metrics. thoughts?

anika: +1 to regional CP for latency-sensitive tenants. question: how do we do cert rollout without peering churn?

sam: We could use mTLS with short-lived certs issued by central CA. agents pull new certs via S3 presigned + signed nonce.

ella: Concern: S3 presigned won't work for air-gapped private deployments. need offline bootstrap path.

jamie: Right — plan: 1) hosted: presigned S3 path 2) dedicated: private controlplane mirroring + internal CA 3) on-prem: bundle + operator. put in doc.

devon: For peering, do we prefer route-based (VPC peering / AWS RAM) vs private endpoint proxies? Tradeoffs: routing cost vs NAT/egress complexity.

anika: Route-based is simpler for lower tenancy counts. For high multi-tenancy, relays avoid exploding route tables.

sam: Relay box approach increases egress IP management but gives better tenancy isolation.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for cp-split/proxy v1 -> infra/region-us-east-1

jamie: Proposed handshake flow (short):
```
1) Agent boot -> contact regional CP pub endpoint
2) CP issues temp token + cert signing request
3) Agent presents CSR to central CA over TLS
4) CA returns leaf cert + agent policy
5) CP creates mapping: agent_id -> tenant CIDR
```

anika: Two questions: how do we protect the CSR step from replay? and how to revoke quickly on compromise?

sam: CSR step requires proof of possession (challenge nonce signed with agent keypair) and we keep revocation list in central DB pushed to CPs.

ella: Revocation distribution via gossip or periodic sync? realtime is preferred for security incidents.

jamie: We'll push revocations via a small pubsub channel over our existing relay mesh; CP nodes subscribe and apply immediately.

devon: Ops: need runbook to force revoke + detach routes. Also need rollback plan if CP-side cert rotation causes mass disconnect.

anika: Rollback idea: dual-cert acceptance window (accept old+new for 10m) and staggered rotation per region.

sam: For BGP/route table scale — if per-tenant routes blow up, fallback to NAT relay for older tenants. Autoswitch policy based on route count.

ella: DNS mapping: prefer per-tenant subdomains, but avoid creating millions of records. Use wildcard + header SNI mapping in proxy.

jamie: Implementation notes: control plane config snippet (conceptual):
```
controlplane:
  auth_provider: central-ca
  relay_policy:
    threshold_routes: 250
    fallback: nat-relay
  cert_rotation_window: 10m
```

anika: Security: KMS integration for central CA keys, HSM recommended for enterprise customers.

devon: Cost: peering + NAT gw egress charges per region. Need cost model for routing vs relay. I'll run numbers.

infra-bot: monitor-bot: cp-split rollout metric: auth-latency p50 increased 7% in canary, error-rate stable.

jamie: 7% okay if p99 unchanged. we should watch for bursts. plan: continue canary 4h, then 2-stage rollout.

sam: Next steps: produce RFC followup with diagrams + runbook. I'll draft and ping for review.

ella: I'll add the on-prem bootstrap flow and revoke playbook.

anika: +1, also add a small test harness to simulate a compromised agent and measure time-to-revoke.

devon: I'll add a cost comparison sheet and include expected egress delta per 1000 tenants.

jamie: Great. No blockers. If infra-bot shows any anomalies, we abort. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary completed for cp-split/proxy v1 -> infra/region-us-east-1 :white_check_mark:

sam: pulling the draft RFC into docs/rfcs/cp-split-handshake.md and will link here shortly.

anika: acked. keeping an eye on metrics :eyes:
